subject.title: Bug: OpenClaw 2026.4.9 exposes agent internal thinking (English) to user

question: Should the security-sensitive remaining fix be handled as a narrow embedded streaming scanner sync under this issue, or folded into the broader reasoning/default leak work?
rationale: The source gap is narrow, but it affects user-visible channel delivery and the live issue is explicitly marked for maintainer and security review with no new fix PR.

options.title: Fix the core streaming scanner now
options.body: Update the embedded streaming scanner or reuse the shared parser so attribute-bearing reasoning tags cannot leak before final sanitization, then add focused regression coverage.

options.title: Fold into broader leak work
options.body: Treat this as part of the open broader reasoning/default and intermediate-text leak cluster if maintainers want one coordinated security hardening change.

options.title: Wait for live transport proof
options.body: Keep this open but defer code work until a maintainer obtains WeChat or another channel proof for the exact streaming attribute-tag leak.

recommendation.title: Fix the core streaming scanner now
recommendation.body: Update the embedded streaming scanner or reuse the shared parser so attribute-bearing reasoning tags cannot leak before final sanitization, then add focused regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The likely decision is about thinking/default behavior and security handling, and steipete has the recent thinking refactor history cited by the report.
